content:
In Tim Cook's final earnings call before officially stepping down as Apple's CEO, artificial intelligence became the hot topic. The investment community is both focused on the potential of Siri AI to stimulate iPhone upgrades and concerned about what this means for Apple's continuously rising capital expenditure costs.

Cook hinted that the financial outlook for Siri AI remains unclear, but casually mentioned that heavy users of Siri AI will face an iCloud+ subscription paywall.

Siri AI is positioned as a free feature within the iPhone, iPad, and Mac operating systems, but it is essentially a service, as Apple needs to continuously invest funds to operate it. Depending on the requested content, the related large language model queries are sent to Apple's own cloud and third-party cloud infrastructure for processing.

Apple publicly hinted for the first time that Siri AI will have a paid component. Although the specific usage cap has not yet been announced, Cook has stated that users cannot use Siri AI for free indefinitely. When usage reaches a certain level, usage will be restricted, and heavy users of the new Siri system will need to purchase the iCloud+ plan.

Augusto Galindo's most-liked comment:

I really can't think of any situation in which you would become a heavy user of Siri AI. It doesn't have the capabilities of OpenAI's or Claude's most powerful models, and it also lacks the related tools.

Of course, the devil is in the details. How many times can you use Siri AI for free before hitting the quota limit? We still don't know at this stage.

The company previously pointed out that new image generation features (such as the "Clean Up" and "Expand" tools in iOS 27 "Photos", as well as the revamped Image Playground app) will have usage caps, while iCloud+ subscribers will enjoy higher usage caps. In the current developer beta and public beta, these limits have not been enabled... so we still don't know how generous the allowances will be at this stage.

Similarly, the new Apple Intelligence feature for video recording in the "Home" app requires the 2TB iCloud plan to use. The new Cloud Pro model access in the "Shortcuts" app is also limited to higher-tier iCloud+ users.

iOS 27 equipped with Siri AI requires iOS devices or Macs that support Apple Intelligence, and will launch later this year. For iPhones, this means iPhone 15 Pro or later models. Due to regulatory restrictions, Siri AI will not be available in Europe or China in the foreseeable future.
